About me

My name is Arwiss Qarnee Wijaya Bin Mohd Soufhwee, a student in Mathematic 1. This portfolio represents my learning outcomes and insights gained from Computational Thinking in Mathematics (MTES 1142).

Beyond standard mathematical concepts, this subject offers a powerful framework for critical thinking and strategic problem-solving. It challenges us to rethink traditional methodologies and adopt a more structured, analytical mindset.

I invite you to explore this portfolio to see how computational thinking can revolutionize our approach to mathematical challenges.

Conclusion & Reflection

Conclusion

Computational thinking in Mathematics is very important in producing students who develop systematic, logical, creative and evaluative ways of thinking to understand. Through the activities presented in this portfolio, I learned how concepts such as decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, algorithms, logical reasoning, and evaluation can be applied to solve mathematical problems. The use of Scratch also makes learning more engaging by providing visual feedback and allowing students to explore mathematical concepts interactively. Overall, computational thinking not only helps in finding answers but also improves the way we understand and approach mathematical problems.

Reflection

For the reflection, I gained a better understanding of how computational thinking can be applied to mathematics. At first, I viewed mathematics mainly as a subject that required following formulas and steps. However, this project showed me that breaking a problem into smaller parts, identifying patterns, choosing important information, following logical steps, and evaluating the answer can make problem-solving easier.
